clue.text: Small drinks on behalf of church team taking orders

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
ales are beers, so drinks
doing something for someone is doing it on their behalf
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church side, refreshed with a few small beers, lining up to receive instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking orders' sounds like a priest's ordination, fitting the church; here it means a firm's staff booking customers' purchases.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's sellers form a team whose job is to win and book customer purchases.

clue.text: Abrasive guide appears around North Dakota

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit around the state abbreviation
to guide is to steer or direct, so the letters are steered into a new order

parts.note: ND is the postal abbreviation for the US state North Dakota

explanation.surface: A rough tour guide turns up around North Dakota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guide' rearranges the letters of 'appears', the word it steers; 'Abrasive' is a noun here, the rubbing material.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandpaper is coarse paper used to rub surfaces smooth, the standard abrasive.

clue.text: Decline rent at university

parts.note: to let is to rent out a property
up means at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Rents at the university go down.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessening or slackening of effort or intensity is a decline.

clue.text: The French turning up cut down outside support under their own steam

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: les is French for 'the' in the plural

indicators.note: the word for cut down sits outside the support word

parts.note: felled means cut down, as a tree
a prop is a support

explanation.surface: The French, turning up, cut down the timber around a support, all by their own power.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving by one's own power, without outside help, is to go under one's own steam.

clue.text: Love to live in credit some weeks

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: the words to and live go in the credit abbreviation

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Love must live on credit for some weeks.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example: the month runs a few weeks.
explanation.definitionFit: A month of the calendar spans a little over four weeks, so it is some weeks.

clue.text: Maybe Jersey Beer erected plant

parts.note: a Jersey is a breed of dairy cow

indicators.note: in a down clue, erected means the word is stood upright, read bottom to top

parts.note: pils is short for Pilsner, a lager beer

explanation.surface: Perhaps Jersey beer was put up in a factory plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey' looks like the Channel Island; 'Maybe' makes it an example of a cow breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a yellow-flowered wild primula, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Junk plans to head west

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means reading right to left, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: maps are plans or charts of an area

explanation.surface: Throw-away plans for a journey westward.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwanted bulk email is called by this name, so it is junk mail.

clue.text: ID of superior doctor in NW London area

indicators.note: the superior and doctor letters go inside the suburb's name

parts.note: Pinner is a suburb in north-west London
U means upper-class, superior, in British usage
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: Identity papers of a senior doctor living in a northwest London suburb.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal identification code entered at cash machines verifies one's identity.

clue.text: Perfect lines to fill little volume

indicators.note: to fill means the poem goes inside the measure

parts.note: ml, millilitre, is a small measure of volume
an ode is a poem, lines of verse

explanation.surface: Perfect lines of verse to fill a slim book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little volume' looks like a slim book but is ML, the millilitre.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, a model pupil or citizen is an ideal, perfect example.

clue.text: Brief message backing TV fundraiser Henry's left

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the remaining letters are read backwards
something that has left is gone, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: a telethon is a long television broadcast raising money for charity
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance; 'Henry's left' is read as Henry has left

explanation.surface: A short note supporting a charity broadcast, mentioning that Henry has departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' removes H from TELETHON, giving TELETON; 'backing' then turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded sheet for writing short letters or thank-you notes.

clue.text: Got up tired, having lost energy

indicators.note: having lost means one letter has gone missing from the word

parts.note: weakened means worn down or tired
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone rose from bed, still exhausted and drained of vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: To be roused from sleep is to have risen from slumber; both mean stirred into consciousness.

clue.text: Bouncer to try to win dodgy hearing

parts.note: a kangaroo bounds along, so it is a bouncer
to court is to woo, trying to win someone over

explanation.surface: A nightclub bouncer tries his luck at a rigged tribunal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' suggests a doorman; it is the hopping animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An unofficial tribunal that ignores justice is an unfair, dodgy trial or hearing.

clue.text: Temporary pianos evenly sited round old university

indicators.note: the pianos sit round each of the other letters in turn
the pianos are spaced out evenly with the other letters slotted between them

parts.note: p is the musical marking for piano, softly; plural pianos gives several of them

explanation.surface: A makeshift arrangement of pianos placed at regular intervals around an old college.
explanation.walkthrough: Three P's are interleaved with O and U: P, O, P, U, P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop-up shop or event is set up for a short time only, so it is temporary.

clue.text: Like interpreter to invoice hosts in August, on returning

indicators.note: hosts means the invoice word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: to bill someone is to send them an invoice

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation for August is read backwards

parts.note: AUG is the abbreviation for the month August

explanation.surface: An interpreter sends a bill for work done in August, on getting back.
explanation.definitionFit: An interpreter must speak two languages fluently to translate between them.

clue.text: Head of printing house fetched back painter (not English) behind picture book

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
back means the word for fetched is read backwards

parts.note: got means fetched, as in went and got it

indicators.note: not means a letter is missing from the painter's name

parts.note: Raphael was the Italian Renaissance painter
a bum is a person's behind, the backside

explanation.surface: A print-shop boss collected a painting by an artist, not an English one, to go behind a picture book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns round the word for fetched, and 'not' drops the E from the painter; 'behind' is British slang for the bottom, not a position.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of photographs is a picture book in which snapshots are kept.

clue.text: Composer on holiday with another, eating nut

indicators.note: the two words eat the nut, holding it inside

parts.note: off means away from work, on holiday
Bach is another composer
en is the printing unit, the half-em, called a nut by printers

explanation.surface: A composer on holiday with a colleague, munching on a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Offenbach wrote operettas such as Orpheus in the Underworld, so he was a composer.

clue.text: Eddy, top conductor, hogging large mike

indicators.note: hogging means keeping something to oneself, so the conductor holds the letter

parts.note: a maestro is a great conductor
M is mike in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Eddy, a leading conductor, keeps grabbing the big microphone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eddy' looks like a man's name; it is a whirlpool.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool, a large swirling eddy of water.

clue.text: Varied resources here to cover French study update

indicators.note: to cover means the rearranged letters wrap round the abbreviation
varied means changed around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Assorted materials here are meant to cover French, as part of updating one's studies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Varied' rearranges RESOURCES HERE, and 'to cover' wraps those letters round FR.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief training course that brings someone's knowledge up to date is a study update.

clue.text: Unfortunate Tory leader packed in spring summit

indicators.note: packed in means these letters are stuffed inside the spring word

parts.note: to hop is to spring
ill means unlucky, as in ill-starred

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An unlucky Conservative leader gets packed off in spring to a summit meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summit' looks like a political meeting; it is the top of a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point of a rise of land is its summit.

clue.text: Some sailor upset pest controller

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: part means some of something
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: Some sailor gets upset by the pest control man.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap for catching rodents is a device that controls pests.

clue.text: A hundred and fifty European books, romantic?

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
lit, short for literature, means books

explanation.surface: A collection of a hundred and fifty European books, perhaps a romantic one?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a dinner by soft flame is the classic romantic setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner lit only by wax tapers is the stock example of a romantic evening.

clue.text: Coconut oil prepared right away, primarily from this

definitions.text: Coconut oil prepared right away, primarily from this

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the first letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: Coconut oil is made straight away, chiefly from this product.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the initials of five words spell the dried kernel that the oil is pressed from.
explanation.definitionFit: Copra is dried coconut kernel, the raw material from which coconut oil is extracted.

clue.text: ''Jaws'' bound to be shown in empty cinemas

definitions.note: chops are the jaws or mouth, as in licking one's chops

indicators.note: shown in means placed inside the outer letters
an empty word keeps only its outside letters

parts.note: to bound is to leap or hop

explanation.surface: The film Jaws is sure to be screened in deserted cinemas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jaws' in quotes looks like the shark film, but it means the mouth; 'empty' keeps just the outside letters of cinemas.
explanation.definitionFit: Chops is informal for the jaws or mouth of a person or animal.

clue.text: Buff coach horse every so often

indicators.note: every so often means taking letters at regular intervals, every second one

explanation.surface: An enthusiast for coaching horses now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buff' looks like an enthusiast; it is a yellowish-brown colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is a yellowish-brown earth pigment, close to the dull yellow shade called buff.

clue.text: Salute archbishop opening mine

indicators.note: the archbishop's name opens up the word for mine, sitting inside it

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I

explanation.surface: An archbishop opens a new mine and receives a salute.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaudit is an expression of praise, a salute or tribute to someone's achievement.

clue.text: Less smooth make-up runs, hard to stop

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so this letter is put inside

parts.note: rouge is red cosmetic for the cheeks
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Make-up that runs, made hard to stop, leaves the skin less smooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarser in texture means less even or polished, the opposite of smooth.

clue.text: Pine tea chest's contents

indicators.note: the contents of the words are letters held within them

explanation.surface: A pine tea chest and what is inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like the wood of the chest, but it is the verb: to long for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine is to long or yearn for something, as does to hanker after it.

clue.text: Saw old man in a hotel with the general manager

indicators.note: in means the old man sits inside the pair of a and hotel

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
pop is informal for father, one's old man

explanation.surface: A sighting of an old man in a hotel with the general manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a past tense, but it is the noun meaning a wise saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old proverb; this word means a pithy maxim of the same kind.
